beats.narration_text: Jelly Hop is Kiran's game: a jelly cube hops across plates on a dinner table while forks stab down from above. Assignment seven adds two clips. Scoot is the looping cycle: two cells on a Sprite2D, held by a discrete frame track, packed from Kiran's assignment-two scoot art, seven ticks per cell, loop linear. Land is the committing action: two Sprite2D cutouts under Node2D pivots, cut from the idle drawing at row six twenty-two, keyed at frames zero, two, four and eight, loop none.

beats.narration_text: A clip is a saved resource: a length, a loop mode, a step, and tracks. Line eleven names the track's target: a node path, then a property, frame. Line six, loop mode one, is loop linear, over a length of fourteen sixtieths.

beats.act: result: the one-tick hand-off error, found and fixed
beats.narration_text: Same clock, so the expected gap is zero. The first wired run said otherwise. At seven four F E four B five the state test failed: one hundred thirty-two checks, five failures. On a direct LAND to SCOOT switch, scoot showed one tick ahead, a sixtieth of a second, with cell one during an A pose. The probe at F D four D eight five five found why: play on a player already playing gets an extra sixtieth from its own update that tick. Five C zero F B nine A fixed it. Now the same log lines read zero.

props.title: Q3 · Two Clocks, One Tick Apart
props.status: Lines from Kiran's committed files and logs · typeset, not a screenshot
props.source: commits 74fe4b5, fd4d855, 5c0fb9a · CHANGE-BRIEF.md Revision 2 · TEST-REPORT.md A7, "Two clocks"

beats.narration_text: The fix is Revision two. Only when the old clip was land, the new one is scoot, and this is not a resume, line two thirty-two seeks one tick early on the loop. The player's own update then lands it exactly on tick mod fourteen. Every other entry, at line two thirty-four, seeks the plain synced time.

props.title: Q3 · The Hand-off Fix
props.source: godot/features/player/player.gd lines 227–236 · rev c1bbb13 · Godot editor reconstruction, not a screenshot
props.code:
anim.play(want)
	if clip == &"land" and want == &"scoot" and not clip_held:
		# Direct LAND -> SCOOT switch: the AnimationPlayer was already playing land, and its own update
		# later this tick adds 1/60 (fd4d855). Seek one tick earlier on the loop so it lands on the synced time
		# (probe H3, prompt-5e).
		anim.seek(fposmod(_clip_time(want) - 1.0 / CLIP_FPS, anim.get_animation(&"scoot").length), true)
	else:
		anim.seek(_clip_time(want), true)
	clip = want
	clip_held = false

beats.narration_text: Verdict. Both clips play as the brief says: scoot synced to the player's tick, land from frame zero, every interrupt on its predicted tick, and zero ticks between the two clocks after the fix, with no failures in one thirty-five, sixty-two, twenty-nine, one thirty-two and three ninety-seven checks. Kiran wrote the brief and its three revisions, measured the landing and chose the cut, ran the sheet tool, the read-backs, the mutations and both strips, and made every verdict. Claude Code wrote the clips, the scene, the visual layer, the tests, the previews and the scripts, and made this film; Claude in chat drafted commands and prompts. The sheet is Kiran's own assignment-two art, made locally with Stable Diffusion XL Base one point oh, under the CreativeML Open RAIL plus plus M licence. Kiran's next step, in Kiran's words: I'd add a scripted test for pausing during LAND and resuming into SCOOT, the one entry no test covers yet. Shown at revision C one B B B one three.
